title: The Benchmark Incentive Hypothesis: Do RAND-Style Competition Incentives Actually Accelerate Formal Verification Progress?

original_idea.body:
# The Benchmark Incentive Hypothesis: Do RAND-Style Competition Incentives Actually Accelerate Formal Verification Progress?

**Problem:** RAND (2026) recommends government benchmark competitions to accelerate formal verification AI development, analogous to how AIxCC accelerated vulnerability detection from 37% to 86% in one year. Whether this incentive mechanism actually works for formal verification is untested.

**Direction:** Survey the formal verification AI research community on: (a) awareness of RAND's proposal, (b) what incentive structure (prize, challenge, grant) would most accelerate their work, (c) what benchmark would best capture meaningful progress. Synthesize responses into a structured policy recommendation.

**Why it matters:** The AIxCC model is a concrete precedent. Whether it transfers to formal verification depends on which bottlenecks competition incentives address. This analysis would inform RAND's recommendation with empirical evidence from the research community.

**Relevant context:** RAND (Sarma & Fisher 2026) explicitly calls for benchmark competitions. AIxCC ran for two years with $18.5M in prizes. A survey of formal verification researchers would calibrate whether the competition model applies.
